comment: Complete these profiles for existing games as they are inspected. For any NEW game a complete entry is mandatory. comparison is an array of 'existing-id: concrete mechanical distinction'; playtestEvidence should include steps and observed outcomes.

patch-tuesday.genre: Real-time arena survival with automatic weapons and upgrade drafting
playerActions: Move with WASD, arrow keys or a touch drag; weapons fire on their own
Collect dropped patches (experience) by walking over or near them
At each level-up, choose 1 of 3 upgrades: a new weapon or another level of an owned weapon or passive
patch-tuesday.coreLoop: Keep moving through swarms while automatic weapons wear them down, collect the experience they drop, and draft an upgrade at every level so the build can outgrow the rising spawn rate.
patch-tuesday.objective: Survive a three-minute maintenance window, then destroy the Zero-Day boss that appears at 3:00.
patch-tuesday.progression: Level-ups draft from four weapons (Patch Bolt, Firewall aura, Antivirus orbit, Ping Flood shockwave) and five passives, each up to level 5. Threats escalate over time (bugs, then worms from 0:20, trojans from 0:45, ransomware from 1:40) with scripted swarm events at 1:00 and 2:00.
patch-tuesday.failureState: Health reaches zero from contact damage or boss bullets. The run ends with an incident report showing time held and the best record, and Play again restarts from level 1.
distinctiveMechanics: Movement is the only direct input; all damage comes from drafted automatic weapons
A fixed three-minute window with timed swarm events, then a boss phase with radial bullet bursts, minion summons and an enrage below half health
An off-screen pointer with distance to the boss
Longest survival and fastest boss kill are kept per browser
comparison: echo: Echo Vault is manual twin-stick aiming with a dash and a recorded echo ghost that fights beside you across waves; Patch Tuesday has no aiming, dash or echo and is built around drafting automatic weapons against a fixed timer and a boss.
breach-command: Breach Command is turn-based squad tactics with telegraphed enemy intents; Patch Tuesday is continuous real-time movement against swarms.
dbo1-defender: SIM-DBO1 Defender Trainer is a security-awareness decision trainer; Patch Tuesday only shares the IT theme and is a reflex survival game.
playtestEvidence: node tests/playtest-patch-tuesday.mjs plays with real arrow keys and picks level-up cards by key in Chromium on a virtual clock. Before rebalancing, four movement-pattern bots all died between 1:04 and 1:25 at levels 4 to 6, just after the 1:00 swarm; after it, runs lasted 1:19 to 2:05 at levels 7 to 13.
The same script checks pause and resume, game over, Play again, and a phone run with a touch-drag joystick and tapped level-up cards; no page or console errors.
A reactive autopilot (?demo test mode, no invincibility) measures how often a player who dodges reaches and beats the 3:00 boss.
Not yet playtested by a person: pattern bots do not dodge, so they understate what a person can survive.

throughput.genre: Real-time factory automation and logistics on a tile grid
playerActions: Place miners on ore and rotate machines so their output arrow faces the next step
Drag to lay whole lines of conveyor belt; merge belts by running one into the side of another
Place smelters, assemblers (choosing Gear, Wire, Circuit or Motor) and splitters
Inspect a machine to see what it is waiting for or blocked by, then delete and rebuild
Pan and zoom the factory floor
throughput.coreLoop: Build a production line from ore to the hub, use each machine's status light to find where items starve or back up, then add or rebalance miners, smelters and assemblers until the line meets the current milestone.
throughput.objective: Clear seven delivery milestones into the central hub, ending with a sustained-rate quota: hold 30 circuits a minute for a full minute.
throughput.progression: Milestones unlock the smelter, the assembler with the gear recipe, the splitter, the wire, circuit and motor recipes, and express belts. Targets climb from 10 iron ore to 20 motors, then the rate quota; afterwards a sandbox with everything unlocked.
throughput.failureState: There is no game over. Failure is a starved or backed-up line that misses its count; in the final milestone the one-minute hold timer resets to zero whenever the circuit rate drops below 30 a minute.
distinctiveMechanics: Every machine is a single tile that accepts input from any side except its output arrow
General assemblers switch recipe (Gear, Wire, Circuit, Motor) instead of dedicated machines
Splitters deal items left, ahead and right in turn; belts merge by side-loading
A ratio-planning finale measured as a rolling 60-second delivery rate with a hold timer
Per-machine status lights (working, waiting for input, blocked) and a waiting-for inspector
Free building with no money, power or research
comparison: factory-flow: Iron & Logic (outside the arcade, merged in #603) is the closest relative and the same genre. It adds power budgeting, money, research labs and dedicated presses and benches across six shipping contracts; Throughput has none of those, uses switchable general assemblers and splitters, and ends on a sustained-rate quota instead of a shipping total.
buckland-blocks: Buckland Blocks centres on building and crafting by hand; in Throughput the player only designs automated lines that run on their own.
breach-command: Breach Command is turn-based combat on a grid; Throughput is real-time logistics with no enemies.
playtestEvidence: node tests/playtest-throughput.mjs plays the packed game through its real UI in Chromium (tool keys, rotation, clicks, belt drags, Select to verify each placement) with a virtual clock: all seven milestones cleared in about 7.5 minutes of game time (11, 34, 99, 38, 71, 72 and 111 seconds), then the win screen, sandbox, and a reload where Continue restores the factory.
Phone (390x844, touch): tapping tools, placing a belt by tap and dragging the floor all work.
node tests/games.mjs --only throughput loads the packed game from file:// without errors.
Not yet playtested by a person: how long a first-time player needs per milestone is unverified.

kettle-cove.genre: Time-loop dialogue RPG on a walkable tile map
playerActions: Walk the harbour with arrow keys, WASD or tap-to-move
Talk to villagers and examine objects, choosing replies by number or tap
Attempt Charm, Wits and Grit checks rolled on 2d6 with the odds shown
Spend levels on skills, read the notebook, and wait for the next bell
kettle-cove.coreLoop: Within one eight-bell day, decide who to talk to and in what order (each new topic costs a bell), collect clues and items, and use what earlier days taught you to unlock new replies before midnight resets the cove.
kettle-cove.objective: Mend the lighthouse lens, get the lighthouse key and light the lamp before midnight; bring the missing keeper home as well for the best ending.
kettle-cove.progression: Twelve clues and experience persist across days; levels raise Charm, Wits and Grit so failed checks become likelier to pass on a later day. Clues open alternative routes, such as Nell's key or the spare key under the anchor stone.
kettle-cove.failureState: Midnight with the lamp dark resets the day: items, promises and trust are lost and you wake on the morning ferry, keeping only the notebook, skills and experience. A failed skill check is locked until the next day.
distinctiveMechanics: A single repeating day where only knowledge and skills carry over
Six villagers on bell-by-bell schedules (the ferryman only in the morning, Wren in three different places)
Conversations spend time: a new topic costs one of eight bells, so the order of visits matters
Visible-odds 2d6 skill checks that lock for the day on failure
Two endings depending on whether the hidden keeper is found and persuaded
comparison: neathbound: NeathBound is open-ended city exploration with quests, inventory and dice; Kettle Cove is one small harbour replayed as a single repeating day in which only knowledge and skills carry over and every new conversation spends one of eight bells.
lantern-road: Lantern Road is a hex-map road campaign with a party and combat; Kettle Cove has no combat or party and is solved by talking, timing and memory across days.
ptshub-wilds-main: Whispering Wilds is a typed-command text adventure with attack and rest; Kettle Cove is a walkable tile map with menu dialogue, NPC schedules and no combat.
playtestEvidence: node tests/playtest-kettle-cove.mjs drives the real UI in Chromium (arrow keys, E, number keys) with a virtual clock: Day 1 talks to the ferryman, Ada, Wren (twice), the cottage, Teodor and Dot, reaching 10 of 12 clues by bell 8; waiting past bell 8 shows the midnight screen and Day 2 starts on the ferry with items reset.

Day 2: the whistle reveals that Old Mosk is Gus, who agrees to come home; Wren, the cottage, Teodor's two-bell lens, Nell's key and the lighthouse lead to 'The Keeper Comes Home' with 11 of 12 clues at level 5. No page or console errors.
Not yet playtested by a person: pacing and how clear the hints are remain unverified.
